blocks.costs: requests per second may fall: your floor is 2.48 (10% below run 20261016T172703Z-bb04's 2.76), and this run made 2.76; throughput worsens (fewer steps per second); TPOT worsens (each step takes longer, as the GPU idles while the CPU plans it); the flag is set at engine start
blocks.name: no-async-scheduling
blocks.reason: prefill took 386 ms per request, about 3.7 decode steps of 103 ms. With async scheduling the next step is already planned when a request arrives, so it waits one extra step; with it off, it joins the next step. Measured once on a T4 with Qwen3-4B, not a prediction for this GPU: turning it off cut prefill from 310 to 164 ms per request while each step grew from 117 to 122 ms
blocks.test: about 7 min on this setup (this run: 166 s to load, a 120 s window planned)

blocks.costs: does not change TTFT (prefill is unchanged); helps throughput and TPOT; TPOT rises when answers do not copy the prompt, and at high concurrency; a slower start
blocks.name: ngram-speculation
blocks.reason: prompts are long (median 495 words beyond what they share). N-gram speculation drafts tokens by copying spans of the prompt, so it only helps when answers quote or repeat their input; otherwise it costs a little - compare TPOT with and without it. Replaying prompt lookup on this run's answers, drafts would supply 9.2% of all output tokens; measure it: the step overhead on this model is not known
